page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c2d server family. It is equipped with 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance features dedicated CPU allocation with 2 threads per core, a 32 MB L3 cache, and 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing it in the top 25% of its class. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and memory bandwidth metrics consistently fall within the average range. For example, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is measured at 62.15 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches 39.95 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also demonstrate average throughput, with Redis handling 8.97 million operations per second. Large language model inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to the bottom 25% for prompt processing on medium 7B models.

The c2d-highmem-8 instance offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. Its dedicated AMD EPYC cores and high memory density make it suitable for database operations, memory-cached web serving, and moderate data processing tasks. However, the lack of local storage and lower multi-core scaling relative to larger instances in the same family represent key tradeoffs for highly parallelized or storage-heavy applications.
